author: Ellen G. White
text: the Father and Son carried out their purpose … to make man in their own image … And now God says to his Son, “Let us make man in our image.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: After God created man in His image, the form was perfect in all its arrangements, but it had no vitality. Then a personal, self-existing God breathed into that form the breath of life

author: Ellen G. White
text: Though formed from the dust, Adam was “the son of God.”

author: Ellen G. White
text: I asked Jesus if his Father had a form like himself. He said he had

author: Uriah Smith
text: Here is an express declaration that God has a person, and of that person Christ is the express image.

author: Ellen G. White
text: The mighty power that works through all nature … is not, as some men of science claim, merely an all-pervading principle, an actuating energy. God is a spirit; yet He is a personal being, for man was made in His image.

author: Ellen G. White
text: Man was to bear God’s image, both in outward resemblance and in character. Christ alone is “the express image” (Hebrews 1:3) of the Father; but man was formed in the likeness of God. His nature was in harmony with the will of God. His mind was capable of comprehending divine things.

author: Ellen G. White
text: God’s character is revealed in the precepts of His law… It is a transcript of God’s character

author: E. J. Waggoner
text: God’s law is the verbal picture of his pure and holy character, it is an expression of the love that springs naturally from his heart.

author: Ellen G. White

author: Ellen G. White
text: Face-to-face, heart-to-heart communion with his Maker

author: J. N. Loughborough
work: An Examination of the Scripture Testimony Concerning Man's Present Condition
text: The foregoing testimony settles the point, that the image of God does not refer to character but to form.
